topic: Template Specialization and SFINAE for Overload Resolution
explanation:
In C++, template specialization allows developers to define custom implementations of a template for specific types or conditions, enabling tailored behavior. Substitution Failure Is Not An Error (SFINAE) is a technique that leverages template specialization and overload resolution to enable or disable template instantiations based on compile-time conditions. Together, these features facilitate writing highly generic, efficient, and type-safe code that adapts to different types or traits without runtime overhead.

In C++, template specialization and SFINAE (Substitution Failure Is Not An Error) enable developers to create flexible, type-dependent behaviors within template classes and functions. This allows the compiler to select the most appropriate implementation based on template parameters, facilitating compile-time polymorphism, type traits, and optimized code paths. These features are essential for writing generic, efficient, and type-safe code in modern C++.
